title: 500MW data center project planned outside San Diego, California
html:
A new data center is being planned in California close to the border with Mexico.

First reported by local press, including KPBS and ABC, a data center development known as Project Eco is being proposed near Jacumba Hot Springs in San Diego County.

Set on 177 acres, the project could total 500MW at full build-out. Spanish renewable energy firm Ignis is reportedly the company behind the development. Site plans suggest the project could include two data center buildings and a battery energy storage system.

Jacumba is about 70 miles (112km) east of the city of San Diego, near the US-Mexico border. The proposed site is north of Interstate 8 at 1425 Carrizo Creek Road, close to an existing substation and solar farm.

The site is owned by Derik Martin, who is set to sell the land to Ignis Energy USA LLC.

News of the project was revealed through a freedom of information request to the county.

An Ignis spokesperson told local press the project is still in the planning stage.

“We have not done an application, so this project right now is nothing more than a consultation to the county to assess what the permitting path will be, to assess whether there are any limitations that are in place for this project,” Tahir Fazal said.

Founded in 2015, Ignis is a Spanish renewable firm with more than 1GW of owned generation capacity either in operation or under construction, managing a total of 10GW of owned and third-party assets.
summary: Spanish renewable firm Ignis behind project
